name: Donald Trump
summary: Trump is a right-populist and nationalist Republican whose program centers on tariffs and trade protection, mass deportation and restricted immigration, deregulation and tax cuts, fossil-fuel expansion, a larger military, and an assertive use of executive power. He treats social issues in a conservative direction (two sexes, an end to DEI, abortion left to states) while having shifted over time on several of them. In foreign policy he combines skepticism of international bodies and allies with unilateral force and territorial ambitions.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Said in 1999 he believed in universal health care, but as a candidate called the ACA a disaster and favored a free-market system; his first-term effort sought to repeal it and the 2024 platform stresses choice and competition.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Signed the 2017 tax cuts, campaigned on making them permanent, and the 2025 law extended them; his tax record points toward lower, not higher, taxes on the wealthy.

property-fundamental.rationale: Called eminent domain 'wonderful' in 2015 and repeatedly asked government to use it for his projects, which suggests he does not see property as very hard to override; ambiguous.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The 2024 platform pledges to cut regulations that 'stifle' jobs and innovation and to reinstate first-term deregulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Signed a 2025 law adding Medicaid and SNAP work requirements and cutting over $1.2 trillion mainly from those programs; he did not frame it as dependency in the sources read.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Backed a fentanyl blockade and military action against cartels and opposed recreational marijuana legalization in 2015 (supported decriminalization in Florida in 2024); said in 1990 drugs should be legalized, which he later dropped.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Platform pledges to bar federal collusion in censoring lawful speech and to protect free speech online; he said he would 'bring back free speech'. No support for hate-speech laws found.

strong-leader.rationale: Said in 2025 'I have the right to do anything I want to do' and governs by emergency declarations and executive orders, saying an emergency 'means you can do whatever you have to do'.

state-harmful.rationale: Uses state power extensively (deportations, tariffs, federal deployments) and seeks a more powerful state in these areas; no anti-state position.

limit-guns.rationale: Platform defends the right to keep and bear arms; he called concealed carry 'a right, not a privilege' and pledged no more gun-free zones.

empower-police-military.rationale: Platform calls to replenish police departments, shield officers from lawsuits and make the military the most powerful in the world; the 2025 law added about $150 billion for defense.

rehabilitation.rationale: Signed the First Step Act in his first term, but is strongly punitive elsewhere (death penalty, 'lock up violent offenders'); mixed.

traditional-family.rationale: Platform promotes a culture that values 'the Sanctity of Marriage' and restoring parental rights in education.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Said in 2011 he opposed it, but after Obergefell said it was 'settled in the Supreme Court... I'm fine with that'; his later campaigns said he supported it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Calls himself pro-life with exceptions; platform leaves it to the states and opposes late-term abortion while backing birth control and IVF; said six weeks is too short.

more-religion-public.rationale: Platform backs students' right to pray and read the Bible in school and creates a federal task force on anti-Christian bias; he credits God for his survival.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Ordered an end to federal DEI and 'environmental justice' offices and preferences, and pledged a 'colorblind and merit-based' society.

gender-social-construct.rationale: His executive order says the U.S. recognizes two immutable sexes and that gender identity is a 'fully internal and subjective sense of self'; inaugural: 'only two genders'.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Platform pledges to 'Honor American History' and reinstate patriotic civics; inaugural calls on Americans not to forget 'our Constitution, and our God'.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Platform and orders: complete the wall, 'largest deportation operation in American history', end chain migration, prioritize merit-based entry; 2025 law funded about $170 billion for border security.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Withdrew the U.S. from the WHO, UNESCO and the Paris accord, and told UN delegates their countries were 'going to hell'; criticizes the UN's irrelevance.

free-trade.rationale: Imposed broad tariffs, says trade deficits harm the U.S., and pledged to 'overhaul' the trade system; he withdrew from the TPP.

nation-first.rationale: 'America First' governance: tariffs 'to enrich our citizens', closure of USAID and withdrawal from international bodies.

open-borders.rationale: Declared a national emergency at the southern border and condemned open borders in Europe as 'suicidal'.

limit-growth.rationale: Inaugural 'drill, baby, drill'; platform ends restrictions on oil, gas and coal and the Green New Deal.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Called climate change a 'con job' at the UN and 'a hoax' earlier; withdrew from the Paris accord twice.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Platform lists nuclear among energy sources to unleash, and the 2025 law adds a bonus credit for nuclear.

central-planning.rationale: Record is deregulation, tax cuts and market-oriented policy; platform attacks the 'Socialist Green New Deal'.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Platform backs baseline tariffs on foreign goods and the Reciprocal Trade Act; he said tariffs would boost domestic manufacturing.

separate-church-state.rationale: Wants a larger public role for religion: a federal anti-Christian-bias task force and school prayer and Bible reading.

military-superiority.rationale: Pledged to 'build the strongest military the world has ever seen'.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Executive order states the principle 'guarantees equality of opportunity, not equal outcomes'.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Repeatedly said he wants Greenland, the Panama Canal ('we're taking it back') and Canada, and said Greenland 'should be controlled by the United States'.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Platform: 'We will stand with Israel'; first term recognized Jerusalem as the capital and brokered the Abraham Accords; he backed Israel in the Gaza war and in the 2026 Iran war.

school-vouchers.rationale: Platform supports 'Universal School Choice in every State'; he backed $20 billion toward vouchers.

force-without-un.rationale: Ordered strikes on Iran, Yemen, Caribbean drug boats and an operation to capture Maduro without UN Security Council approval.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Signed a law requiring Medicaid recipients aged 19-64 to work, volunteer or study 80 hours a month, and extended SNAP work rules to ages 18-64.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Platform: 'DRILL, BABY, DRILL', energy dominance, end restrictions on oil, gas and coal.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: English-language order says a national language is 'at the core of a unified and cohesive society'; he said 'this is a country where we speak English'.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Inaugural promises to 'restore the integrity, competency, and loyalty' of government, implying a view that it lacked them.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Orders speak of serving 'every person with equal dignity and respect', though policy sharply differentiates by citizenship status.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Platform backs students' right to pray and read the Bible in school, which is not the same as state religious instruction.

death-penalty.rationale: Executive order directs the Attorney General to 'pursue the death penalty for all crimes of a severity demanding its use' and seek overruling of limiting precedents.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Order tries to deny birthright citizenship to children of unlawfully present or temporary-status parents, tying citizenship to parental status; it does not touch children of citizens or permanent residents.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Platform pledges to defend religious liberty; no specific position on exemptions for minorities found.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Closed USAID, froze most foreign aid and cut aid to South Africa.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Tried to fire Fed governor Lisa Cook and has pressed for faster rate cuts, as the Justice Department probed Powell.

collective-defense.rationale: Threatened not to defend allies who miss spending targets, avoided endorsing Article 5, and asked in 2026 why the U.S. spends on allies 'not there for us'.

space-expansion.rationale: Pledged to plant the flag on Mars and prioritizes Moon and Mars missions; a central goal is not his stated framing.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Ended federal DEI programs and prefers merit-based selection; no mandate for parity.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Platform pledges to reinstate the 1776 Commission and 'Honor American History'.

patriotic-education.rationale: Platform: reinstate the 1776 Commission and 'Fair and Patriotic Civics Education'.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Orders ending federal race and gender preferences and set-asides; aims for a 'colorblind and merit-based' society.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Platform pledges to stop China from buying American industries and real estate.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Platform promises 'no cuts, including no changes to the retirement age' to Social Security; no push for private accounts.

single-official-language.rationale: Designated English the official language in 2025, but the order leaves agencies free to keep providing services in other languages.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Platform seeks to stop China buying American real estate; no blanket ban on all foreigners found.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Order calls disparate-impact liability 'wholly inconsistent with the Constitution' and seeks to end it.

non-intervention.rationale: Intervened in Venezuela, struck Iran and Yemen and threatens Greenland; denies no right of intervention.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Platform promotes 'the Sanctity of Marriage'; treats marriage as a protected institution.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Order bars federal recognition of gender identity, requires sex-based designation of spaces and forms, and platform bans funding for gender surgeries.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Wants the strongest military in the world and added $150 billion in defense spending.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Platform: replenish police departments and 'lock up violent offenders'.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Order defines sex as an 'immutable biological classification' and defines male and female by reproductive cells.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Order protects self-custody of digital assets and use of open blockchains 'without persecution'; does not address untraceability.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Ordered offensive strikes and a regime-change war on Iran and an operation to capture Maduro.

arms-reduction.rationale: Seeks the strongest military and added about $150 billion in defense spending; platform wants the most lethal force.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Rolls back environmental regulation and rejects climate-driven limits.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: English-language order and his remark that 'we speak English, not Spanish'; no explicit requirement for immigrants found.

voter-id.rationale: Platform supports voter ID, proof of citizenship and paper ballots.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Authorized lethal strikes on alleged drug-trafficking boats and calls cartels terrorists; this is close to but not exactly killing suspects 'without trial' on land.

close-ties-china.rationale: Platform revokes China's Most Favored Nation status and phases out imports of essential Chinese goods; he escalated the trade war.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Frames tariffs as protecting 'American workers and families' and enriching citizens.

notes: Positions are taken from his mature, recent record (2024-2026) where views changed: he said in 1999 he was 'very pro-choice' and believed in universal health care and in 2004 identified more as a Democrat. Most economic-philosophy, constitutional-design, religious and radical-ideology statements have no recorded position and are null. Minimum wage and estate-tax positions were reported only through search snippets that were not opened, so they are left null. Several 2026 events come from Wikipedia and a PBS report and should be rechecked.
